sanskrit: agrataḥ prayayau rāmaḥ sītā madhye sumadhyamā pṛṣṭhatas tu dhanuṣpāṇir lakṣmaṇo 'nujagāma ha
english: Rāma went in front, the slender-waisted Sītā in the middle, and Lakṣmaṇa, bow in hand, followed behind.

sanskrit: tau paśyamānau vividhāñ śailaprasthān vanāni ca nadīś ca vividhā ramyā jagmatuḥ saha sītayā
english: The two of them, beholding various mountain plateaus, forests, and lovely rivers of every kind, journeyed on together with Sītā.

sanskrit: sārasāṃś cakravākāṃś ca nadīpulinacāriṇaḥ sarāṃsi ca sapadmāni yutāni jalajaiḥ khagaiḥ
english: They saw sārasa cranes and cakravāka birds roaming the sandy river banks, and lotus-covered lakes teeming with water-birds.

sanskrit: yūthabaddhāṃś ca pṛṣatān madonmattān viṣāṇinaḥ mahiṣāṃś ca varāhāṃś ca gajāṃś ca drumavairiṇaḥ
english: They saw spotted deer moving in herds, rutting-mad horned animals, buffaloes, wild boars, and elephants that are the enemies of trees.

sanskrit: te gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ lambamāne divākare dadṛśuḥ sahitā ramyaṃ taṭākaṃ yojanāyatam
english: Traveling a long way, as the sun descended, they together beheld a beautiful lake extending a full yojana.

sanskrit: padmapuṣkarasaṃbādhaṃ gajayūthair alaṃkṛtam sārasair haṃsakādambaiḥ saṃkulaṃ jalacāribhiḥ
english: It was crowded with lotuses and blue water-lilies, graced by herds of elephants, and filled with sārasa cranes, haṃsas, kādamba ducks, and other water-fowl.

sanskrit: prasannasalile ramyatasmin sarasi śuśruve gītavāditranirghoṣo na tu kaś cana dṛśyate
english: From that beautiful lake with its clear waters, the sounds of song and music were heard, yet nothing could be seen.

sanskrit: tataḥ kautūhalād rāmo lakṣmaṇaś ca mahārathaḥ muniṃ dharmabhṛtaṃ nāma praṣṭuṃ samupacakrame
english: Then, out of curiosity, Rāma and the great warrior Lakṣmaṇa approached the sage named Dharmabhṛt to inquire.

sanskrit: idam atyadbhutaṃ śrutvā sarveṣāṃ no mahāmune kautūhalaṃ mahaj jātaṃ kim idaṃ sādhu kathyatām
english: "Having heard this most wondrous thing, great curiosity has arisen in all of us, O great sage. Please explain well what this is."

sanskrit: tenaivam ukto dharmātmā rāghaveṇa munis tadā prabhāvaṃ sarasaḥ kṛtsnam ākhyātum upacakrame
english: Thus addressed by the righteous Rāghava, that sage of virtuous soul then began to relate the full glory of the lake.

sanskrit: idaṃ pañcāpsaro nāma taṭākaṃ sārvakālikam nirmitaṃ tapasā rāma muninā māṇḍakarṇinā
english: "This lake, O Rāma, is named Pañcāpsaras and is eternal; it was created through the austerities of the sage Māṇḍakarṇi."

sanskrit: sa hi tepe tapas tīvraṃ māṇḍakarṇir mahāmuniḥ daśavarṣasahasrāṇi vāyubhakṣo jalāśraya
english: "For the great sage Māṇḍakarṇi had practiced severe austerities for ten thousand years, subsisting on air alone, standing in water."

sanskrit: tataḥ pravyathitāḥ sarve devāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ abruvan vacanaṃ sarve paraspara samāgatāḥ asmakaṃ kasya cit sthānam eṣa prārthayate muniḥ
english: "Then all the gods, headed by Agni, were alarmed and, gathering together, said to one another: 'This sage is seeking the position of one among us.'"

sanskrit: tataḥ kartuṃ tapovighnaṃ sarvair devair niyojitāḥ pradhānāpsarasaḥ pañcavidyuccalitavarcasaḥ
english: "Then, commissioned by all the gods to obstruct his austerity, five chief apsarases, their splendor flickering like lightning, were sent."

sanskrit: apsarobhis tatas tābhir munir dṛṣṭaparāvaraḥ nīto madanavaśyatvaṃ surāṇāṃ kāryasiddhaye
english: "By those apsarases, the sage who knew past and future was then brought under the sway of Kāma, for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose."

sanskrit: tāś caivāpsarasaḥ pañcamuneḥ patnītvam āgatāḥ taṭāke nirmitaṃ tāsām asminn antarhitaṃ gṛham
english: "Those five apsarases became the sage's wives, and their hidden dwelling was built in this lake."

sanskrit: tatraivaāpsarasaḥ pañcanivasantyo yathāsukham ramayanti tapoyogān muniṃ yauvanam āsthitam
english: "There those five apsarases, dwelling at ease, delight the sage who, though devoted to austerity, retains the vigor of youth."

sanskrit: tāsāṃ saṃkrīḍamānānām eṣa vāditraniḥsvanaḥ śrūyate bhūṣaṇonmiśro gītaśabdo manoharaḥ
english: "As they sport, this sound of instruments mixed with the jingling of ornaments and the delightful sound of singing is heard."

sanskrit: āścaryam iti tasyaitad vacanaṃ bhāvitātmanaḥ rāghavaḥ pratijagrāha saha bhrātrā mahāyaśāḥ
english: Calling it wonderful, the illustrious Rāghava, along with his brother, accepted the account of that purified soul.

sanskrit: evaṃ kathayamānasya dadarśāśramamaṇḍalam kuśacīraparikṣiptaṃ nānāvṛkṣasamāvṛtam
english: While he was thus narrating, they beheld a hermitage precinct enclosed by kuśa grass and bark-cloth garments and surrounded by various trees.

sanskrit: praviśya saha vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca rāghavaḥ tadā tasmin sa kākutsthaḥ śrīmaty āśramamaṇḍale
english: Kākutstha Rāghava then entered that beautiful hermitage precinct along with Vaidehī and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: uṣitvā susukhaṃ tatra pūrjyamāno maharṣibhiḥ jagāma cāśramāṃs teṣāṃ paryāyeṇa tapasvinām
english: Dwelling there in great comfort, honored by the great sages, he visited in turn the hermitages of those ascetics.

sanskrit: yeṣām uṣitavān pūrvaṃ sakāśe sa mahāstravit kva cit paridaśān māsān ekaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ kva cit
english: He, the master of great weapons, had previously stayed near those sages—sometimes for ten months, sometimes for a full year.

sanskrit: kva cic ca caturo māsān pañcaṣaṭ cāparān kva cit aparatrādhikān māsān adhyardham adhikaṃ kva cit
english: Somewhere for four months, elsewhere for five or six, in other places for more than that, and sometimes for more than a year and a half.

sanskrit: trīn māsān aṣṭamāsāṃś ca rāghavo nyavasat sukham tathā saṃvasatas tasya munīnām āśrameṣu vai ramataś cānukulyena yayuḥ saṃvatsarā daśa
english: Rāghava dwelt happily for three months or eight months at a time; dwelling thus in the hermitages of the sages and enjoying himself in all manner of ways, ten years passed for him.

sanskrit: parisṛtya ca dharmajño rāghavaḥ saha sītayā sutīkṣṇasyāśramaṃ śrīmān punar evājagāma ha
english: The illustrious Rāghava, the knower of dharma, after wandering about with Sītā, returned once more to the hermitage of Sutīkṣṇa.

sanskrit: sa tam āśramam āgamya munibhiḥ pratipūjitaḥ tatrāpi nyavasad rāmaḥ kaṃ cit kālam ariṃdamaḥ
english: Arriving at that hermitage, honored by the sages, Rāma the subduer of enemies dwelt there for some time.

sanskrit: athāśramastho vinayāt kadā cit taṃ mahāmunim upāsīnaḥ sa kākutsthaḥ sutīkṣṇam idam abravīt
english: Then, residing in the hermitage, on one occasion Kākutstha humbly approached that great sage, and seated beside Sutīkṣṇa, spoke thus:

sanskrit: asminn araṇye bhagavann agastyo munisattamaḥ vasatīti mayā nityaṃ kathāḥ kathayatāṃ śrutam
english: "O venerable one, I have always heard from storytellers that the foremost of sages, Agastya, dwells in this forest."

sanskrit: na tu jānāmi taṃ deśaṃ vanasyāsya mahattayā kutrāśramapadaṃ puṇyaṃ maharṣes tasya dhīmataḥ
english: "But on account of the vastness of this forest, I do not know in what place the holy hermitage of that wise great sage lies."

sanskrit: prasādāt tatra bhavataḥ sānujaḥ saha sītayā agastyam abhigaccheyam abhivādayituṃ munim
english: "By your grace, I would go with my brother and with Sītā to pay reverence to the sage Agastya."

sanskrit: manoratho mahān eṣa hṛdi saṃparivartate yad ahaṃ taṃ munivaraṃ śuśrūṣeyam api svayam
english: "This great wish turns over in my heart—that I might myself serve that best of sages."

sanskrit: iti rāmasya sa muniḥ śrutvā dharmātmano vacaḥ sutīkṣṇaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ prīto daśarathātmajam
english: Hearing these words of the righteous Rāma, the sage Sutīkṣṇa, delighted, replied thus to the son of Daśaratha:

sanskrit: aham apy etad eva tvāṃ vaktukāmaḥ salakṣmaṇam agastyam abhigaccheti sītayā saha rāghava
english: "I too was wishing to tell you precisely this—go to Agastya, together with Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tv idānīm arthe 'smin svayam eva bravīṣi mām aham ākhyāmi te vatsa yatrāgastyo mahāmuniḥ
english: "By good fortune you yourself speak to me of this matter now. I shall tell you, dear one, where the great sage Agastya dwells."

sanskrit: yojanāny āśramāt tāta yāhi catvāri vai tataḥ dakṣiṇena mahāñ śrīmān agastyabhrātur āśramaḥ
english: "Go four yojanas from the hermitage, dear one; then to the south lies the great and beautiful hermitage of Agastya's brother."

sanskrit: sthalaprāye vanoddeśe pippalīvanaśobhite bahupuṣpaphale ramye nānāśakuninādite
english: "In a mostly dry forest region, beautiful with a grove of pippalī trees, abundant with flowers and fruits, lovely, resounding with various birds—

sanskrit: padminyo vividhās tatra prasannasalilāḥ śivāḥ haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇāś cakravākopaśobhitāḥ
english: "—there are various lotus pools with clear, auspicious waters, thronged with haṃsas and kāraṇḍava ducks, graced by cakravāka birds."

sanskrit: tatraikāṃ rajanīm uṣya prabhāte rāma gamyatām dakṣiṇāṃ diśam āsthāya vanakhaṇḍasya pārśvataḥ
english: "Having passed one night there, O Rāma, set out in the morning, taking the southern direction along the flank of the forest tract."

sanskrit: tatrāgastyāśramapadaṃ gatvā yojanam antaram ramaṇīye vanoddeśe bahupādapa saṃvṛte raṃsyate tatra vaidehī lakṣmaṇaś ca tvayā saha
english: "Proceeding thence for one yojana, you will reach Agastya's hermitage in a delightful forest region thickly covered with trees; there Vaidehī and Lakṣmaṇa will delight in dwelling with you."

sanskrit: sa hi ramyo vanoddeśo bahupādapasaṃkulaḥ yadi buddhiḥ kṛtā draṣṭum agastyaṃ taṃ mahāmunim adyaiva gamane buddhiṃ rocayasva mahāyaśaḥ
english: "For that forest region is charming and dense with many trees. If you have decided to see that great sage Agastya, resolve to depart this very day, O greatly illustrious one."

sanskrit: iti rāmo muneḥ śrutvā saha bhrātrābhivādya ca pratasthe 'gastyam uddiśya sānujaḥ saha sītayā
english: Hearing this from the sage, Rāma paid homage to him along with his brother, and set out toward Agastya with his younger brother and Sītā.

sanskrit: paśyan vanāni citrāṇi parvapāṃś cābhrasaṃnibhān sarāṃsi saritaś caiva pathi mārgavaśānugāḥ
english: Beholding wondrous forests and mountain peaks resembling clouds, and lakes and rivers as they came along the path,

sanskrit: sutīkṣṇenopadiṣṭena gatvā tena pathā sukham idaṃ paramasaṃhṛṣṭo vākyaṃ lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: traveling comfortably by the path indicated by Sutīkṣṇa, greatly joyful, he spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: etad evāśramapadaṃ nūnaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ agastyasya muner bhrātur dṛśyate puṇyakarmaṇaḥ
english: "This must indeed be the hermitage of the holy-actioned brother of the great-souled sage Agastya, which is now visible."

sanskrit: yathā hīme vanasyāsya jñātāḥ pathi sahasraśaḥ saṃnatāḥ phalabhareṇa puṣpabhāreṇa ca drumāḥ
english: "For behold—the trees of this forest, recognizable on the path in their thousands, are bent low with the weight of fruits and the load of blossoms."

sanskrit: pippalīnāṃ ca pakvānāṃ vanād asmād upāgataḥ gandho 'yaṃ pavanotkṣiptaḥ sahasā kaṭukodayaḥ
english: "This fragrance wafted from this forest by the wind is the suddenly arising pungent scent of ripened pippalī fruits."

sanskrit: tatra tatra ca dṛśyante saṃkṣiptāḥ kāṣṭhasaṃcayāḥ lūnāś ca pathi dṛśyante darbhā vaidūryavarcasaḥ
english: "Here and there are visible neatly gathered piles of wood; and along the path one sees cut darbha grass with the luster of vaidūrya gems."

sanskrit: etac ca vanamadhyasthaṃ kṛṣṇābhraśikharopamam pāvakasyāśramasthasya dhūmāgraṃ saṃpradṛśyate
english: "And in the midst of the forest, resembling the peak of a dark cloud, the tip of smoke from the fire of the resident ascetics is clearly visible."

sanskrit: vivikteṣu ca tīrtheṣu kṛtasnānā dvijātayaḥ puṣpopahāraṃ kurvanti kusumaiḥ svayam ārjitaiḥ
english: "At secluded tīrthas, twice-born ones who have bathed are making flower offerings with blossoms gathered by themselves."

sanskrit: tat sutīkṣṇasya vacanaṃ yathā saumya mayā śrutam agastyasyāśramo bhrātur nūnam eṣa bhaviṣyati
english: "This must indeed be the hermitage of Agastya's brother, just as I heard it described in Sutīkṣṇa's words, O gentle one."

sanskrit: nigṛhya tarasā mṛtyuṃ lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā yasya bhrātrā kṛteyaṃ dik śaraṇyā puṇyakarmaṇā
english: "This is the direction made safe and sheltering by that one's brother, who with great power suppressed death out of desire for the welfare of the worlds, through his holy deeds."

sanskrit: ihaikadā kila krūro vātāpir api celvalaḥ bhrātarau sahitāv āstāṃ brāhmaṇaghnau mahāsurau
english: "Here, it is said, the cruel Vātāpi and also Ilvala, two great demons who were killers of brāhmaṇas, once dwelt together as brothers."

sanskrit: dhārayan brāhmaṇaṃ rūpam ilvalaḥ saṃskṛtaṃ vadan āmantrayati viprān sa śrāddham uddiśya nirghṛṇaḥ
english: "Ilvala, assuming the form of a brāhmaṇa and speaking the refined language, would mercilessly invite brāhmaṇas under the pretext of a śrāddha."

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ saṃskṛtaṃ bhrātā tatas taṃ meṣarūpiṇam tān dvijān bhojayām āsa śrāddhadṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: "Then the brother, after transforming his brother into the form of a ram, would feed those twice-born guests with him according to the rite of the śrāddha."

sanskrit: tato bhuktavatāṃ teṣāṃ viprāṇām ilvalo 'bravīt vātāpe niṣkramasveti svareṇa mahatā vadan
english: "After those brāhmaṇas had eaten, Ilvala would call out in a loud voice: 'Vātāpi, come forth!'"

sanskrit: tato bhrātur vacaḥ śrutvā vātāpir meṣavan nadan bhittvā bhitvā śarīrāṇi brāhmaṇānāṃ viniṣpatat
english: "Then Vātāpi, hearing his brother's call, bleating like a ram, would tear through the bodies of the brāhmaṇas and burst forth."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ sahasrāṇi tair evaṃ kāmarūpibhiḥ vināśitāni saṃhatya nityaśaḥ piśitāśanaiḥ
english: "By those two flesh-eating shape-shifters operating together in this way, thousands of brāhmaṇas were constantly destroyed."

sanskrit: agastyena tadā devaiḥ prārthitena maharṣiṇā anubhūya kila śrāddhe bhakṣitaḥ sa mahāsuraḥ
english: "Then the great sage Agastya, implored by the gods, having partaken of the śrāddha, ate that great demon."

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃpannam ity uktvā dattvā hastāvasecanam bhrātaraṃ niṣkramasveti ilvalaḥ so 'bhyabhāṣata
english: "Then, after saying 'The meal is complete' and performing the hand-rinsing rite, Ilvala spoke thus: 'Brother, come forth.'"

sanskrit: taṃ tathā bhāṣamāṇaṃ tu bhrātaraṃ vipraghātinam abravīt prahasan dhīmān agastyo munisattamaḥ
english: "But to that brother speaking thus—the slayer of brāhmaṇas—the wise Agastya, foremost of sages, replied with a smile:"

sanskrit: kuto niṣkramituṃ śaktir mayā jīrṇasya rakṣasaḥ bhrātus te meṣa rūpasya gatasya yamasādanam
english: "'How can your brother, now digested by me, have the power to come forth—the demon in the form of a ram who has gone to the abode of Yama?'"

sanskrit: atha tasya vacaḥ śrutvā bhrātur nidhanasaṃśritam pradharṣayitum ārebhe muniṃ krodhān niśācaraḥ
english: "Then, hearing those words announcing his brother's death, the night-roving demon, in his rage, began to assail the sage."

sanskrit: so 'bhyadravad dvijendraṃ taṃ muninā dīptatejasā cakṣuṣānalakalpena nirdagdho nidhanaṃ gataḥ
english: "He charged at that foremost of twice-born ones, but was utterly consumed by the blazing-glorious sage with a glance like fire, and met his death."

sanskrit: tasyāyam āśramo bhrātus taṭākavanaśobhitaḥ viprānukampayā yena karmedaṃ duṣkaraṃ kṛtam
english: "This is the hermitage of his brother, graced by a lake and forest—he by whose compassion for brāhmaṇas this difficult deed was done."

sanskrit: evaṃ kathayamānasya tasya saumitriṇā saha rāmasyāstaṃ gataḥ sūryaḥ saṃdhyākālo 'bhyavartata
english: As Rāma thus narrated, together with the son of Sumitrā, the sun set and the hour of twilight came.

sanskrit: upāsya paścimāṃ saṃdhyāṃ saha bhrātrā yathāvidhi praviveśāśramapadaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ cābhyavādayan
english: Having observed the western twilight rite with his brother according to the prescribed manner, he entered the hermitage and paid homage to that sage.

sanskrit: samyak pratigṛhītas tu muninā tena rāghavaḥ nyavasat tāṃ niśām ekāṃ prāśya mūlaphalāni ca
english: Properly received by that sage, Rāghava spent that one night there, having partaken of roots and fruits.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ vimale sūryamaṇḍale bhrātaraṃ tam agastyasya āmantrayata rāghavaḥ
english: When that night had passed and the disk of the sun was bright, Rāghava addressed that brother of Agastya:

sanskrit: abhivādaye tvā bhagavan sukham adhyuṣito niśām āmantraye tvāṃ gacchāmi guruṃ te draṣṭum agrajam
english: "I pay you reverence, O venerable one; I have dwelt here in comfort through the night. I take my leave of you; I go to see your elder brother, my preceptor."

sanskrit: gamyatām iti tenokto jagāma raghunandanaḥ yathoddiṣṭena mārgeṇa vanaṃ tac cāvalokayan
english: Told 'You may go' by him, the delight of Raghu's line departed, beholding that forest as he went along the indicated path.

sanskrit: nīvārān panasāṃs tālāṃs timiśān vañjulān dhavān ciribilvān madhūkāṃś ca bilvān api ca tindukān
english: He saw nīvāra grasses, jackfruit trees, palms, timiśa, vañjula, dhava, ciribilva, madhūka, bilva, and tinduka trees—

sanskrit: puṣpitān puṣpitāgrābhir latābhir anuveṣṭitān dadarśa rāmaḥ śataśas tatra kāntārapādapān
english: —trees in bloom, wound about by creepers with flowering tips, Rāma beheld by the hundreds in that wilderness.

sanskrit: hastihastair vimṛditān vānarair upaśobhitān mattaiḥ śakunisaṃghaiś ca śataśaḥ pratināditān
english: He saw trees uprooted by elephant trunks, graced by monkeys, and resounding in their hundreds with flocks of intoxicated birds.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt samīpasthaṃ rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nugataṃ vīraṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ lakṣmivardhanam
english: Then the lotus-eyed Rāma spoke to the heroic Lakṣmaṇa, increaser of prosperity, who followed close behind:

sanskrit: snigdhapatrā yathā vṛkṣā yathā kṣāntā mṛgadvijāḥ āśramo nātidūrastho maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ
english: "Just as the trees have glossy leaves, just as the deer and birds are tame—the hermitage of the great sage of cultivated soul is not far off."

sanskrit: agastya iti vikhyāto loke svenaiva karmaṇā āśramo dṛśyate tasya pariśrānta śramāpahaḥ
english: "Known in the world as 'Agastya's' by his own deeds alone, his hermitage is visible—the remover of fatigue for the weary."

sanskrit: prājyadhūmākulavanaś cīramālāpariṣkṛtaḥ praśāntamṛgayūthaś ca nānāśakunināditaḥ
english: "Its forest filled with abundant smoke, adorned with garlands of bark garments, with herds of deer at rest, and resounding with various birds—

sanskrit: nigṛhya tarasā mṛtyuṃ lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā dakṣiṇā dik kṛtā yena śaraṇyā puṇyakarmaṇā
english: "—this is the hermitage of him who with great power suppressed death for the welfare of the worlds, and by whose holy deeds the southern quarter was made a place of refuge."

sanskrit: tasyedam āśramapadaṃ prabhāvād yasya rākṣasaiḥ dig iyaṃ dakṣiṇā trāsād dṛśyate nopabhujyate
english: "This is his hermitage precinct—by whose power this southern quarter, through fear of him, is not oppressed by rākṣasas."

sanskrit: yadā prabhṛti cākrāntā dig iyaṃ puṇyakarmaṇā tadā prabhṛti nirvairāḥ praśāntā rajanīcarāḥ
english: "From the time this quarter was secured by his holy deeds, from that time the night-roaming demons have been without enmity and at peace."

sanskrit: nāmnā ceyaṃ bhagavato dakṣiṇā dik pradakṣiṇā prathitā triṣu lokeṣu durdharṣā krūrakarmabhiḥ
english: "This southern quarter bears the venerable one's name as 'Agastya's quarter,' renowned in the three worlds as inviolable by those of cruel deeds."

sanskrit: mārgaṃ niroddhuṃ satataṃ bhāskarasyācalottamaḥ saṃdeśaṃ pālayaṃs tasya vindhyaśaulo na vardhate
english: "Obeying his command so as not to constantly obstruct the sun's path, the great Vindhya mountain does not grow."

sanskrit: ayaṃ dīrghāyuṣas tasya loke viśrutakarmaṇaḥ agastyasyāśramaḥ śrīmān vinītamṛgasevitaḥ
english: "This is the beautiful hermitage of long-lived Agastya, famed for his deeds in the world, frequented by tame deer."

sanskrit: eṣa lokārcitaḥ sādhur hite nityaṃ rataḥ satām asmān adhigatān eṣa śreyasā yojayiṣyati
english: "This virtuous one, worshipped by the worlds, ever devoted to the welfare of the good—he will unite us, who have now arrived, with what is most beneficial."

sanskrit: ārādhayiṣyāmy atrāham agastyaṃ taṃ mahāmunim śeṣaṃ ca vanavāsasya saumya vatsyāmy ahaṃ prabho
english: "Here I shall propitiate that great sage Agastya, O gentle one, and I shall dwell here for the remainder of my forest exile, O lord."

sanskrit: atra devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ agastyaṃ niyatāhāraṃ satataṃ paryupāsate
english: "Here gods with gandharvas, siddhas, and supreme sages constantly attend upon Agastya who is disciplined in his diet."

sanskrit: nātra jīven mṛṣāvādī krūro vā yadi vā śaṭhaḥ nṛśaṃsaḥ kāmavṛtto vā munir eṣa tathāvidhaḥ
english: "No liar, no cruel one, nor a rogue, nor a savage man, nor one given to sensual indulgence could live here—such is the power of this sage."

sanskrit: atra devāś ca yakṣāś ca nāgāś ca patagaiḥ saha vasanti niyatāhārā dharmam ārādhayiṣṇavaḥ
english: "Here gods, yakṣas, nāgas together with birds dwell with regulated diet, wishing to worship dharma."

sanskrit: atra siddhā mahātmāno vimānaiḥ sūryasaṃnibhaiḥ tyaktvā dehān navair dehaiḥ svaryātāḥ paramarṣayaḥ
english: "Here supreme sages, great-souled siddhas, having abandoned their bodies and taken new bodies, have gone to heaven in celestial vehicles resembling the sun."

sanskrit: yakṣatvam amaratvaṃ ca rājyāni vividhāni ca atra devāḥ prayacchanti bhūtair ārādhitāḥ śubhaiḥ
english: "Here gods, propitiated by auspicious beings, grant the state of yakṣa, immortality, and various kingdoms."

sanskrit: āgatāḥ smāśramapadaṃ saumitre praviśāgrataḥ nivedayeha māṃ prāptam ṛṣaye saha sītayā
english: "We have arrived at the hermitage precinct; enter first, O son of Sumitrā, and announce to the sage that I have come here with Sītā."

sanskrit: sa praviśyāśramapadaṃ lakṣmaṇo rāghavānujaḥ agastyaśiṣyam āsādya vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Lakṣmaṇa, younger brother of Rāghava, entering the hermitage precinct, approached a disciple of Agastya and spoke these words:

sanskrit: rājā daśaratho nāma jyeṣṭhas tasya suto balī rāmaḥ prāpto muniṃ draṣṭuṃ bhāryayā saha sītayā
english: "There was a king named Daśaratha; his eldest son, the mighty Rāma, has come to see the sage, together with his wife Sītā."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇo nāma tasyāhaṃ bhrātā tv avarajo hitaḥ anukūlaś ca bhaktaś ca yadi te śrotram āgataḥ
english: "I am his younger brother named Lakṣmaṇa, devoted and loyal to him, if you have heard of me."

sanskrit: te vayaṃ vanam atyugraṃ praviṣṭāḥ pitṛśāsanāt draṣṭum icchāmahe sarve bhagavantaṃ nivedyatām
english: "We have entered this most formidable forest by our father's command; we all wish to see the venerable one—please inform him."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā lakṣmaṇasya tapodhanaḥ tathety uktvāgniśaraṇaṃ praviveśa niveditum
english: Hearing those words of Lakṣmaṇa, the sage wealthy in austerities said 'So be it' and entered the fire-chamber to announce the news.

sanskrit: sa praviśya muniśreṣṭhaṃ tapasā duṣpradharṣaṇam kṛtāñjalir uvācedaṃ rāmāgamanam añjasā
english: Entering and joining his palms, he straightforwardly announced to the foremost sage, invincible through his austerities, the arrival of Rāma:

sanskrit: putrau daśarathasyemau rāmo lakṣmaṇa eva ca praviṣṭāv āśramapadaṃ sītayā saha bhāryayā
english: "These two sons of Daśaratha, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, have entered the hermitage precinct together with Sītā, his wife."

sanskrit: draṣṭuṃ bhavantam āyātau śuśrūṣārtham ariṃdamau yad atrānantaraṃ tattvam ājñāpayitum arhasi
english: "They have come, those two subduer of enemies, to see you and to serve you; it is right that you command what should be done next."

sanskrit: tataḥ śiṣyād upaśrutya prāptaṃ rāmaṃ salakṣmaṇam vaidehīṃ ca mahābhāgām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then, having heard from his disciple of the arrival of Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa and the highly blessed Vaidehī, he spoke these words:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā rāmaś cirasyādya draṣṭuṃ māṃ samupāgataḥ manasā kāṅkṣitaṃ hy asya mayāpy āgamanaṃ prati
english: "By good fortune Rāma has come after so long to see me today; for his coming was indeed longed for by me also in my heart."

sanskrit: gamyatāṃ satkṛto rāmaḥ sabhāryaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ praveśyatāṃ samīpaṃ me kiṃ cāsau na praveśitaḥ
english: "Let Rāma be honored and brought in with his wife and Lakṣmaṇa; let him be ushered into my presence. Why has he not already been brought in?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu muninā dharmajñena mahātmanā abhivādyābravīc chiṣyas tatheti niyatāñjaliḥ
english: Addressed thus by the sage, the great-souled knower of dharma, the disciple bowed and said 'Very well,' his hands joined in reverence.

sanskrit: tato niṣkramya saṃbhrāntaḥ śiṣyo lakṣmaṇam abravīt kvāsau rāmo muniṃ draṣṭum etu praviśatu svayam
english: Then the disciple emerged in haste and said to Lakṣmaṇa: 'Where is Rāma? Let him come to see the sage; let him enter himself.'

sanskrit: tato gatvāśramapadaṃ śiṣyeṇa saha lakṣmaṇaḥ darśayām āsa kākutsthaṃ sītāṃ ca janakātmajām
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa went to the hermitage precinct along with the disciple and presented Kākutstha and Sītā, daughter of Janaka.

sanskrit: taṃ śiṣyaḥ praśritaṃ vākyam agastyavacanaṃ bruvan prāveśayad yathānyāyaṃ satkārārthaṃ susatkṛtam
english: The disciple, speaking Agastya's words with due humility, ushered him in properly, with all honor, for the purpose of receiving hospitality.

sanskrit: praviveśa tato rāmaḥ sītayā sahalakṣmaṇaḥ praśāntahariṇākīrṇam āśramaṃ hy avalokayan
english: Then Rāma entered with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, gazing at the hermitage thronged with peaceful deer.

sanskrit: sa tatra brahmaṇaḥ sthānam agneḥ sthānaṃ tathaiva ca viṣṇoḥ sthānaṃ mahendrasya sthānaṃ caiva vivasvataḥ
english: There he saw the altar of Brahman, and likewise the altar of Agni, the altar of Viṣṇu, the altar of Mahendra, and the altar of Vivasvat;

sanskrit: somasthānaṃ bhagasthānaṃ sthānaṃ kauberam eva ca dhātur vidhātuḥ sthānaṃ ca vāyoḥ sthānaṃ tathaiva ca
english: the altar of Soma, the altar of Bhaga, the altar of Kubera, the altar of Dhātṛ, the altar of Vidhātṛ, and likewise the altar of Vāyu;

sanskrit: tataḥ śiṣyaiḥ parivṛto munir apy abhiniṣpatat taṃ dadarśāgrato rāmo munīnāṃ dīptatejasaṃ abravīd vacanaṃ vīro lakṣmaṇaṃ lakṣmivardhanam
english: Then the sage himself came forth surrounded by his disciples; Rāma saw him ahead, blazing with the radiance of sages, and the hero spoke to the prosperity-increasing Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: eṣa lakṣmaṇa niṣkrāmaty agastho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ audāryeṇāvagacchāmi nidhānaṃ tapasām imam
english: "This is the venerable sage Agastya who comes forth, O Lakṣmaṇa; by his majesty I recognize him as the treasury of austerities."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhur agastyaṃ sūryavarcasaṃ jagrāha paramaprītas tasya pādau paraṃtapaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed scorcher of foes, supremely delighted, grasped the feet of sun-radiant Agastya.

sanskrit: abhivādya tu dharmātmā tasthau rāmaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ sītayā saha vaidehyā tadā rāma salakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Having paid reverence, the righteous Rāma stood with joined palms, together with Vaidehī Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca kākutstham arcayitvāsanodakaiḥ kuśalapraśnam uktvā ca āsyatām iti so 'bravīt
english: Receiving Kākutstha and honoring him with a seat and water, and asking after his welfare, Agastya said: 'Be seated.'

sanskrit: agniṃ hutvā pradāyārghyam atithiṃ pratipūjya ca vānaprasthena dharmeṇa sa teṣāṃ bhojanaṃ dadau
english: Having offered oblations to the fire, presented the arghya offering, and honored the guest, he gave them food according to the dharma of a forest-dweller.

sanskrit: prathamaṃ copaviśyātha dharmajño munipuṃgavaḥ uvāca rāmam āsīnaṃ prāñjaliṃ dharmakovidam
english: Then the foremost sage, the knower of dharma, having first seated himself, spoke to Rāma who sat with joined palms, that expert in dharma:

sanskrit: anyathā khalu kākutstha tapasvī samudācaran duḥsākṣīva pare loke svāni māṃsāni bhakṣayet
english: "Truly, O Kākutstha, an ascetic who behaves otherwise—not properly receiving a guest—would in the next world eat his own flesh like a false witness."

sanskrit: rājā sarvasya lokasya dharmacārī mahārathaḥ pūjanīyaś ca mānyaś ca bhavān prāptaḥ priyātithiḥ
english: "A king of all the worlds who walks in dharma, a great warrior—you are a beloved guest deserving of worship and honor who has arrived."

sanskrit: evam uktvā phalair mūlaiḥ puṣpaiś cānyaiś ca rāghavam pūjayitvā yathākāmaṃ punar eva tato 'bravīt
english: Having spoken thus and honored Rāghava as desired with fruits, roots, flowers, and other things, he then spoke again:

sanskrit: idaṃ divyaṃ mahac cāpaṃ hemavajravibhūṣitam vaiṣṇavaṃ puruṣavyāghra nirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā
english: "This divine and mighty bow, adorned with gold and diamond, belonging to Viṣṇu, O tiger among men, was fashioned by Viśvakarman—

sanskrit: amoghaḥ sūryasaṃkāśo brahmadattaḥ śarottamaḥ datto mama mahendreṇa tūṇī cākṣayasāyakau
english: "—this supreme arrow, infallible, bright as the sun, given by Brahman; and these two quivers of inexhaustible arrows were given to me by Mahendra—

sanskrit: saṃpūrṇau niśitair bāṇair jvaladbhir iva pāvakaiḥ mahārājata kośo 'yam asir hemavibhūṣitaḥ
english: "—filled with sharp arrows blazing like fire; and this great silver scabbard, and this sword adorned with gold—

sanskrit: anena dhanuṣā rāma hatvā saṃkhye mahāsurān ājahāra śriyaṃ dīptāṃ purā viṣṇur divaukasām
english: "—with this bow, O Rāma, having slain great demons in battle, Viṣṇu in former times took the resplendent glory of the heaven-dwellers."

sanskrit: tad dhanus tau ca tūṇīrau śaraṃ khaḍgaṃ ca mānada jayāya pratigṛhṇīṣva vajraṃ vajradharo yathā
english: "Accept this bow, those two quivers, the arrow, and the sword for victory, O giver of honor, as the thunderbolt-holder accepts his bolt."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejāḥ samastaṃ tad varāyudham dattvā rāmāya bhagavān agastyaḥ punar abravīt
english: Having spoken thus, the greatly glorious venerable Agastya, after giving all those excellent weapons to Rāma, spoke again:

sanskrit: rāma prīto 'smi bhadraṃ te parituṣṭo 'smi lakṣmaṇa abhivādayituṃ yan māṃ prāptau sthaḥ saha sītayā
english: "O Rāma, I am pleased; good fortune to you; O Lakṣmaṇa, I am fully content that you have come to pay reverence to me together with Sītā."

sanskrit: adhvaśrameṇa vāṃ khedo bādhate pracuraśramaḥ vyaktam utkaṇṭhate cāpi maithilī janakātmajā
english: "The fatigue of the road afflicts you two greatly; and evidently Maithilī, daughter of Janaka, also yearns for comfort."

sanskrit: eṣā hi sukumārī ca duḥkhaiś ca na vimānitā prājyadoṣaṃ vanaṃ praptā bhartṛsnehapracoditā
english: "For she is delicate and not unaccustomed to hardships; yet she has reached the forest with its many adversities, impelled by her love for her husband."

sanskrit: yathaiṣā ramate rāma iha sītā tathā kuru duṣkaraṃ kṛtavaty eṣā vane tvām anugacchatī
english: "Arrange it so that Sītā may find delight here, O Rāma; she has done what is difficult, following you in the forest."

sanskrit: eṣā hi prakṛtiḥ strīṇām āsṛṣṭe raghunandana samastham anurajyante viṣamasthaṃ tyajanti ca
english: "For this is the nature of women, O delight of Raghu's line, innate since creation: they love a man when he is prosperous and abandon him when he is in adversity."

sanskrit: śatahradānāṃ lolatvaṃ śastrāṇāṃ tīkṣṇatāṃ tathā garuḍānilayoḥ śaighryam anugacchanti yoṣitaḥ
english: "Women follow the fickleness of lightning, the sharpness of weapons, and the swiftness of Garuḍa and the wind."

sanskrit: iyaṃ tu bhavato bhāryā doṣair etair vivarjitāḥ ślāghyā ca vyapadeśyā ca yathā devī hy arundhatī
english: "But this wife of yours is free from these faults, praiseworthy and worthy of acclaim, just as the goddess Arundhatī herself."

sanskrit: alaṃkṛto 'yaṃ deśaś ca yatra saumitriṇā saha vaidehyā cānayā rāma vatsyasi tvam ariṃdama
english: "And this region will be adorned by the place where you, O subduer of foes, will dwell with the son of Sumitrā and with this Vaidehī."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu muninā rāghavaḥ saṃyatāñjaliḥ uvāca praśritaṃ vākyam ṛṣiṃ dīptam ivānalam
english: Thus addressed by the sage, Rāghava, with joined palms, spoke humble words to the sage who blazed like a fire:

sanskrit: dhanyo 'smy anugṛhīto 'smi yasya me munipuṃgavaḥ guṇaiḥ sabhrātṛbhāryasya varadaḥ parituṣyati
english: "I am blessed, I am favored—the foremost of sages, the granter of boons, is fully satisfied with the virtues of me together with my brother and wife."

sanskrit: kiṃ tu vyādiśa me deśaṃ sodakaṃ bahukānanam yatrāśramapadaṃ kṛtvā vaseyaṃ nirataḥ sukham
english: "But do indicate to me a region with water and many forests, where I might establish a hermitage and dwell in contentment."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn muni śreṣṭhaḥ śrutvā rāmasya bhāṣitam dhyātvā muhūrtaṃ dharmātmā dhīro dhīrataraṃ vacaḥ
english: Then the foremost sage, hearing Rāma's words, reflecting for a moment, the righteous and resolute one spoke words yet more resolute:

sanskrit: ito dviyojane tāta bahumūlaphalodakaḥ deśo bahumṛgaḥ śrīmān pañcavaṭy abhiviśrutaḥ
english: "Two yojanas from here, dear one, is a region abounding in roots, fruits, and water, rich with many animals, beautiful, celebrated as Pañcavaṭī."

sanskrit: tatra gatvāśramapadaṃ kṛtvā saumitriṇā saha ramasva tvaṃ pitur vākyaṃ yathoktam anupālayan
english: "Going there, establishing a hermitage with the son of Sumitrā, take your delight, keeping faithfully to your father's word as it was spoken."

sanskrit: vidito hy eṣa vṛttānto mama sarvas tavānagha tapasaś ca prabhāvena snehād daśarathasya ca
english: "For this entire history of yours is known to me, O sinless one, both through the power of my austerities and through my affection for Daśaratha."

sanskrit: hṛdayasthaś ca te chando vijñātas tapasā mayā iha vāsaṃ pratijñāya mayā saha tapovane
english: "And the wish dwelling in your heart has been discerned by me through austerity—the desire to reside here in this forest of austerities with me."

sanskrit: ataś ca tvām ahaṃ brūmi gaccha pañcavaṭīm iti sa hi ramyo vanoddeśo maithilī tatra raṃsyate
english: "Therefore I tell you: go to Pañcavaṭī; for that forest region is lovely, and Maithilī will delight there."

sanskrit: sa deśaḥ ślāghanīyaś ca nātidūre ca rāghava godāvaryāḥ samīpe ca maithilī tatra raṃsyate
english: "That region is praiseworthy, not too far, O Rāghava, and near the Godāvarī; Maithilī will delight there."

sanskrit: prājyamūlaphalaiś caiva nānādvija gaṇair yutaḥ viviktaś ca mahābāho puṇyo ramyas tathaiva ca
english: "Abundant in roots and fruits, filled with various flocks of birds, secluded, O mighty-armed one, holy and lovely as well—

sanskrit: bhavān api sadāraś ca śaktaś ca parirakṣaṇe api cātra vasan rāmas tāpasān pālayiṣyasi
english: "—and you too, together with your wife and capable of protection, dwelling there, O Rāma, will protect the ascetics."

sanskrit: etad ālakṣyate vīra madhukānāṃ mahad vanam uttareṇāsya gantavyaṃ nyagrodham abhigacchatā
english: "This great grove of madhuka trees is visible, O hero; one must go to the north of it, heading toward the nyagrodha tree."

sanskrit: tataḥ sthalam upāruhya parvatasyāvidūrataḥ khyātaḥ pañcavaṭīty eva nityapuṣpitakānanaḥ
english: "Then ascending the high ground not far from the mountain, one reaches the forest perpetually in bloom, renowned as Pañcavaṭī itself."

sanskrit: agastyenaivam uktas tu rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha sātkṛtyāmantrayām āsa tam ṛṣiṃ satyavādinam
english: Thus addressed by Agastya, Rāma together with the son of Sumitrā took proper leave of that truth-speaking sage.

sanskrit: tau tu tenābhyanujñātau kṛtapādābhivandanau tadāśramāt pañcavaṭīṃ jagmatuḥ saha sītayā
english: The two of them, granted leave by him and having made obeisance at his feet, set out from that hermitage toward Pañcavaṭī together with Sītā.

sanskrit: gṛhītacāpau tu narādhipātmajau viṣaktatūṇī samareṣv akātarau yathopadiṣṭena pathā maharṣiṇā prajagmatuḥ pañcavaṭīṃ samāhitau
english: The two sons of the lord of men, having taken up their bows, with quivers fastened on, fearless in battle, proceeded with collected minds toward Pañcavaṭī by the path indicated by the great sage.
